cannibalisation_check.verdict: No cannibalisation of the target keyword: no page of ours targets 'travel advisor wedding', 'destination wedding travel agent' or 'why use a travel advisor'. /travel is the commercial page for the same offer; this article supports it, links to it and must not duplicate its inclusions list. Write the article.

cross_market_insights: No editorial page answers the query in any city. Page one is directories (wezoree, WedAdvisor, National Wedding Directory, Melbourne Wedding and Bride, Airtasker, Kompass B2B lists), agency homepages and service pages with no snippet, social posts, and two US posts from 2018 and 2020 (travel-bash.com) with a generic 'save time, money and stress' line.

The only on-intent Australian content is vowsafar.au comparing a planning platform with a travel agency. Nobody explains what a travel advisor actually does for a wedding: room blocks and attrition, flights for a group, guest transfers, elderly guests, honeymoon sequencing, what happens when a flight is cancelled, or how advisors are paid.

Destination wedding travel agent SERP is strongly commercial: 5 top ads (including a blocked marketplace promising 'one point of contact'), local packs of high-street agencies in all three cities. The luxury, accountable, one-team angle is contested in ads but not in organic content.

PAA is about planners and budgets (planner cost, realistic destination wedding budget, cheaper or not), not about travel advisors. The reader's real question is 'is it worth it, and what does it cost us'.

Australians search 'travel agent', not 'travel advisor' (all measurable AU volume uses 'agent'). Use 'travel advisor' in the H1 as the user chose, but explain the terms early and use 'travel agent' in an H2 and FAQs.
payload.recommended_angle: A travel advisor is the person who makes 80 people, three flights, two hotels and a honeymoon work as one trip, and who answers the phone when a flight is cancelled. Show the invisible work (room blocks, cut-off dates, rooming lists, transfers, elderly guests, honeymoon sequencing), what partner-property benefits really are and how to read them, how advisors are paid and what to ask, and who does what between a travel advisor, a wedding planner and a concierge. Nobody ranking does any of this for Australian couples.
